q: Plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose glucose and oxygen. This process is called ____.
e: Plants use carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll and light to compose glucose and oxygen. This process is called photosynthesis. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: Photosynthesis takes place in the ____ of the green parts of plants but mainly in the leaves.
e: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of the green parts of plants but mainly in the leaves. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: Most green parts of a plant can photosynthesize but the ____ are best adapted for this function.
e: Most green parts of a plant can photosynthesize but the leaves are best adapted for this function. Leaves is the biological term this statement needs.

q: For photosynthesis efficiency, leaves need to have a large surface area to absorb light, much chlorophyll to catch the light, veins including xylem and phloem to supply water and a system for carrying away the ____ to other parts of the plant.
e: For photosynthesis efficiency, leaves need to have a large surface area to absorb light, much chlorophyll to catch the light, veins including xylem and phloem to supply water and a system for carrying away the photosynthetic products to other parts of the plant. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened.

q: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by ____ which support the leaf blade to be angled to receive the maximum amount of sunlight.
e: Most leaves are thin, flat structures supported by petiole which support the leaf blade to be angled to receive the maximum amount of sunlight. The petiole holds the leaf blade at an angle that catches light.

q: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called ____.
e: The tissue between the upper and lower epidermis is called mesophyll. Mesophyll is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The ____ mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many chloroplasts.
e: The palisade mesophyll cells are usually long and contain many chloroplasts. Palisade mesophyll is packed with chloroplasts near the upper surface of the leaf. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: The ____ mesophyll cells vary in shape and are loosely arranged with many air spaces between them.
e: The spongy mesophyll cells vary in shape and are loosely arranged with many air spaces between them. Spongy mesophyll has air spaces that help gases move through the leaf. Leaf air spaces connect stomata to mesophyll so gases can diffuse.

q: The major vein of the leaf is called the ____ continuation of petiole from which the veins are branched off as a network throughout the leaf surface.
e: The major vein of the leaf is called the midrib continuation of petiole from which the veins are branched off as a network throughout the leaf surface. The petiole holds the leaf blade at an angle that catches light.

q: Vascular bundles are existed in the petiole, midrib and veins. They consist of two different tissues: xylem and ____.
e: Vascular bundles are existed in the petiole, midrib and veins. They consist of two different tissues: xylem and phloem. Phloem carries sugars away from the leaf to the rest of the plant. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and thick walled ____.
e: In xylem, vessels are cylindrical, hollow and thick walled cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Xylem brings water and minerals up to the photosynthetic cells.

q: The phloem consists of sieve tubes which are elongated cells and the transverse walls of sieve tubes are perforated ____.
e: The phloem consists of sieve tubes which are elongated cells and the transverse walls of sieve tubes are perforated sieve plates. Phloem carries sugars away from the leaf to the rest of the plant.

q: The epidermis helps to keep the leaf's shape and to reduce water loss. The epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through. Chloroplasts are ____.
e: The epidermis helps to keep the leaf's shape and to reduce water loss. The epidermal cells are thin to allow light to pass through. Chloroplasts are absent. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: It exposes many cells to light rays, photosynthesis takes place mainly in this region.
e: It exposes many cells to light rays, photosynthesis takes place mainly in this region. Mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: It allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells, photosynthesis also takes place in this region.
e: It allows diffusion of carbon dioxide and oxygen in and out of mesophyll cells, photosynthesis also takes place in this region. Mesophyll is the photosynthetic tissue between the upper and lower epidermis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: They consists of vascular bundles (xylem and phloem) and support the leaf. Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by roots to leaves. Phloem transports ____ to other parts of the plant.
e: They consists of vascular bundles (xylem and phloem) and support the leaf. Xylem carries water and minerals absorbed by roots to leaves. Phloem transports photosynthetic products to other parts of the plant. A vascular system of xylem and phloem is missing in bryophytes.

q: It protects inner tissues and reduces the water loss. The stoma is the site of gaseous exchange into and out of the leaf.
e: It protects inner tissues and reduces the water loss. The stoma is the site of gaseous exchange into and out of the leaf. Gaseous exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: ____ is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and other pigments.
e: Chloroplast is a membrane bound organelle containing chlorophyll a, b and other pigments. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy.

q: Plant cells contain chloroplasts which are green in colour. The most important function of chloroplast is to synthesize food by the process of ____.
e: Plant cells contain chloroplasts which are green in colour. The most important function of chloroplast is to synthesize food by the process of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally ____ shaped.
e: Chloroplasts found in higher plants are generally biconvex shaped. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: The parts of a chloroplast are as follows: (a) Outer membrane - It is a semi-porous membrane and is permeable to small molecules and ions which diffuse easily.
e: The parts of a chloroplast are as follows: (a) Outer membrane - It is a semi-porous membrane and is permeable to small molecules and ions which diffuse easily. Membranes are phospholipid bilayers that control transport and keep compartments. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: (b) Intermembrane space - It is a thin space about 10-20 nm and it lies between the outer and the inner membranes of the ____.
e: (b) Intermembrane space - It is a thin space about 10-20 nm and it lies between the outer and the inner membranes of the chloroplast. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: (c) Inner membrane - The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the ____.
e: (c) Inner membrane - The inner membrane of the chloroplast forms a border to the stroma. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma is the chloroplast fluid around the thylakoids.

q: (d) Stroma - Protein rich aqueous fluid is present within the inner membrane of the chloroplast. The space outside the thylakoid is called the ____.
e: (d) Stroma - Protein rich aqueous fluid is present within the inner membrane of the chloroplast. The space outside the thylakoid is called the stroma. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma is the chloroplast fluid around the thylakoids.

q: The chloroplast DNA, ribosomes, the thylakoid system, starch granules and many proteins are found in the ____.
e: The chloroplast DNA, ribosomes, the thylakoid system, starch granules and many proteins are found in the stroma. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. Stroma is the chloroplast fluid around the thylakoids.

q: The stroma is the site for the ____ of photosynthesis.
e: The stroma is the site for the dark reaction of photosynthesis. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process.

q: (e) Thylakoid system - The thylakoids are suspended in the stroma. They are membranous sacs which are arranged in stacks known as ____.
e: (e) Thylakoid system - The thylakoids are suspended in the stroma. They are membranous sacs which are arranged in stacks known as grana. Grana are stacks of thylakoids inside a chloroplast. Thylakoid membranes hold chlorophyll and run the light-dependent reactions.

q: Each granum contains around ____ thylakoids.
e: Each granum contains around 10-20 thylakoids. 10-20 is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the ____ of photosynthesis.
e: The thylakoid membrane is the site for the light reactions of photosynthesis. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis.

q: The green pigment chlorophyll is present on the membrane of ____ in the chloroplast.
e: The green pigment chlorophyll is present on the membrane of thylakoid in the chloroplast. Thylakoid membranes hold chlorophyll and run the light-dependent reactions. Light reactions sit in the thylakoid membrane.

q: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the green portion of light. The other wavelengths of light (blue-480 nm and red-700 nm) are almost totally absorbed by chlorophyll and light energy is transformed into ____.
e: Chlorophyll reflects mostly the green portion of light. The other wavelengths of light (blue-480 nm and red-700 nm) are almost totally absorbed by chlorophyll and light energy is transformed into chemical energy. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells. Chlorophyll is the green pigment that captures light energy.

q: Photosynthesis is the process of conversion of light energy into ____ which can be utilized by the living organisms.
e: Photosynthesis is the process of conversion of light energy into chemical energy which can be utilized by the living organisms. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells. Biological molecules occur naturally inside living organisms, not in bare rock.

q: Photosynthesis comprises of two phases: the light reaction and the ____.
e: Photosynthesis comprises of two phases: the light reaction and the dark reaction. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: The light reaction takes place on the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast and the dark reaction takes place in the ____ of the chloroplast.
e: The light reaction takes place on the thylakoid membrane of chloroplast and the dark reaction takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast. The stroma is the fluid of the chloroplast where the Calvin cycle builds sugar. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: The light reaction is a light-dependent process which includes a series of events such as light absorption, photolysis and release of oxygen and formation of chemical compounds: ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) and ____.
e: The light reaction is a light-dependent process which includes a series of events such as light absorption, photolysis and release of oxygen and formation of chemical compounds: ATP (Adenosine triphosphate) and NADPH. NADPH is the reduced coenzyme that carries high-energy electrons to the Calvin cycle. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: 2H₂O + 2NADP⁺ + 3ADP + 3Pᵢ (phosphate ion) → O₂ + 2NADPH + ____
e: 2H₂O + 2NADP⁺ + 3ADP + 3Pᵢ (phosphate ion) → O₂ + 2NADPH + 3ATP. 3ATP is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The dark reaction is also called ____.
e: The dark reaction is also called Calvin cycle. The Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugar in the stroma. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process.

q: It is a light-independent process in which sugar molecules are formed by using carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and NADPH produced from the ____.
e: It is a light-independent process in which sugar molecules are formed by using carbon dioxide with the help of ATP and NADPH produced from the light reaction. The light reactions split water, release oxygen, and make ATP and NADPH. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: This reaction converts six molecules of carbon dioxide into one sugar molecule i.e. ____.

q: 6CO₂ + 18ATP + 12NADPH → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O + 18ADP + 18Pᵢ + ____
e: 6CO₂ + 18ATP + 12NADPH → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O + 18ADP + 18Pᵢ + 12NADP⁺. 12NADP⁺ is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The light reaction takes place in the presence of ____.

q: The dark reaction takes place in the absence of ____.
e: The dark reaction takes place in the absence of light. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: Light reaction is a ____ phase.
e: Light reaction is a photochemical phase. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. The light reactions split water, release oxygen, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: Dark reaction is a ____ phase.
e: Dark reaction is a biochemical phase. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly.

q: Light reaction occurs in the ____ of the chloroplast.

q: Dark reaction occurs in the ____ of the chloroplast.

e: In the light reaction, NADP utilizes H⁺ ions to form NADPH. NADPH is the reduced coenzyme that carries high-energy electrons to the Calvin cycle. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: In the dark reaction, ____ molecules are formed using CO₂.
e: In the dark reaction, Glucose molecules are formed using CO₂. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process.

q: The end product of the light reaction is ATP and ____.
e: The end product of the light reaction is ATP and NADPH. NADPH is the reduced coenzyme that carries high-energy electrons to the Calvin cycle. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: The end product of the dark reaction is ____.
e: The end product of the dark reaction is Glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process.

q: Photolysis ____ in the light reaction.
e: Photolysis occurs in the light reaction. The light reactions capture photons, split water, and make ATP and NADPH. The light reactions split water, release oxygen, and make ATP and NADPH.

q: Photolysis does not ____ in the dark reaction.
e: Photolysis does not occur in the dark reaction. The dark reaction uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon; it is not a night-only process. The dark reaction, or Calvin cycle, uses ATP and NADPH to make sugar and does not need light directly.

q: The rate of photosynthesis varies according to the controlling factors such as light intensity, temperature and ____ concentration.
e: The rate of photosynthesis varies according to the controlling factors such as light intensity, temperature and carbon dioxide concentration. q: The chemical reaction called respiration is vital for the growth, repair and survival of all ____.

e: As a result, the glucose is not broken down to carbon dioxide and water, but to lactic acid instead. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: During vigorous exercise, oxygen cannot reach the muscles fast enough, so muscle cells carry out ____ respiration.
e: During vigorous exercise, oxygen cannot reach the muscles fast enough, so muscle cells carry out anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Therefore lactic acid builds up in the muscles and blood, and causes the ____.
e: Therefore lactic acid builds up in the muscles and blood, and causes the oxygen debt. Oxygen debt is the extra oxygen needed after anaerobic work to clear lactate. Oxygen debt is repaid after anaerobic muscle work.

q: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the ____.
e: The oxygen debt is removed during recovery by aerobic respiration of lactic acid in the liver. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals. Oxygen debt is repaid after anaerobic muscle work.

q: Lactic acid can slowly poison muscles and cause ____, so it must be removed from the body.
e: Lactic acid can slowly poison muscles and cause cramps, so it must be removed from the body. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. In a fermenter, microbes can be grown rapidly under controlled conditions.

q: After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the ____.
e: After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the liver. The liver stores glycogen, makes bile, and handles many blood chemicals. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. After exercise the heart continues to beat at a fast rate in order to transport lactic acid in the blood from the muscles to the.

q: Lactic acid must be broken down in the liver by breathing faster and deeper in order to supply more ____.
e: Lactic acid must be broken down in the liver by breathing faster and deeper in order to supply more oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short.

q: Some of the lactic acid is oxidized to produce energy. The energy is used to convert the remaining lactic acid to ____.
e: Some of the lactic acid is oxidized to produce energy. The energy is used to convert the remaining lactic acid to glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short.

q: Initially the test tube was filled with mercury hence leaving no room for ____.
e: Initially the test tube was filled with mercury hence leaving no room for oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: The carbon dioxide produced by the seeds must be due to ____ respiration.
e: The carbon dioxide produced by the seeds must be due to anaerobic respiration. Anaerobic respiration or fermentation happens without oxygen and yields little ATP. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: Food contains chemical energy. Respiration is the release of this energy when food, e.g. glucose is broken down in living cells. The energy produced is not used immediately but stored in the mitochondria as a chemical compound called ____.
e: Food contains chemical energy. Respiration is the release of this energy when food, e.g. Glucose is broken down in living cells. The energy produced is not used immediately but stored in the mitochondria as a chemical compound called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

q: ATP is a nucleotide that consists of three main structures: the nitrogenous base, adenine; the pentose sugar, ribose; and a chain of three ____ bound to ribose.
e: ATP is a nucleotide that consists of three main structures: the nitrogenous base, adenine; the pentose sugar, ribose; and a chain of three phosphate groups bound to ribose. A nucleotide is a sugar, a phosphate, and a nitrogen base.

q: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in cytoplasm and absorbs a relatively large amount of energy released from ____.
e: The ATP molecule is formed by bounding adenosine diphosphate to a phosphate group in cytoplasm and absorbs a relatively large amount of energy released from glucose. Glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration. ATP holds usable energy in its phosphate bonds.

q: Thus, respiration is the key physiological process in any living system, providing required energy for other ____.
e: Thus, respiration is the key physiological process in any living system, providing required energy for other processes. Physiological adaptations are internal function changes, such as ADH control of water. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: The energy released from ATP can be used in different forms for many activities. This is summarized below. as solvent for chemical reactions C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Energy (from oxidation glucose) for photosynthesis P ADP → ATP low energy → high energy P Energy for cell activity Using energy The energy released from ATP can be used for a variety of purposes, such as: (a) cell division and ____.
e: The energy released from ATP can be used in different forms for many activities. This is summarized below. As solvent for chemical reactions C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + Energy (from oxidation glucose) for photosynthesis P ADP → ATP low energy → high energy P Energy for cell activity Using energy The energy released from ATP can be used for a variety of purposes, such as: (a) cell division and growth. ATP holds usable energy in its phosphate bonds.

q: (b) synthesis of proteins, fats, vitamins etc.
e: (b) synthesis of proteins, fats, vitamins etc. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: (c) conduction of nerve impulses and muscular ____.
e: (c) conduction of nerve impulses and muscular movements. Movements is the biological term this statement needs.

q: (d) maintenance of constant body ____.
e: (d) maintenance of constant body temperature. Temperature is the biological term this statement needs.

q: (e) active transport of molecules and ____.
e: (e) active transport of molecules and ions. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient.

q: Fill a small vacuum flask with pea seeds which have been soaked in water for 24 hours and rinsed with 1% formalin for 5 minutes. These solutions will kill the bacteria or fungi on the surface of the pea ____.
e: Fill a small vacuum flask with pea seeds which have been soaked in water for 24 hours and rinsed with 1% formalin for 5 minutes. These solutions will kill the bacteria or fungi on the surface of the pea seeds. Electron beams travel in a vacuum, so EM specimens must be specially prepared. Some stages of division are timed in hours in typical cell-cycle descriptions.

q: Kill an equal quantity of soaked pea seeds by boiling them for 5 ____.
e: Kill an equal quantity of soaked pea seeds by boiling them for 5 minutes. Minutes is the biological term this statement needs.

q: After a few days, the temperature in the flask with the living seedlings will be higher than in the control, because heat energy is released during respiration of germinating ____.
e: After a few days, the temperature in the flask with the living seedlings will be higher than in the control, because heat energy is released during respiration of germinating seeds. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are connected through an important ____.
e: Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are connected through an important relationship. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: This relationship enables life to ____.
e: This relationship enables life to survive. Survive is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The products of one process are the ____ of the other.
e: The products of one process are the reactants of the other. Reactants is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Photosynthesis makes the glucose that is used in cellular respiration to make ____.
e: Photosynthesis makes the glucose that is used in cellular respiration to make ATP. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: The glucose is then turned back into carbon dioxide, which is used in ____.
e: The glucose is then turned back into carbon dioxide, which is used in photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: While water is broken down to form oxygen during photosynthesis, in cellular respiration oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form ____.
e: While water is broken down to form oxygen during photosynthesis, in cellular respiration oxygen is combined with hydrogen to form water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: While photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, cellular respiration requires oxygen and releases ____.
e: While photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, cellular respiration requires oxygen and releases carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of ____.
e: Cellular respiration works best in the presence of oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Respiration releases energy from food; do not mix it up with just breathing.

q: Without oxygen, much less ____ would be produced.
e: Without oxygen, much less ATP would be produced. ATP is the cell's immediate energy currency.

q: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis and cellular respiration worldwide helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at ____ levels.
e: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen during photosynthesis and cellular respiration worldwide helps to keep atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide at stable levels. Photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: It occurs only in plants and ____.
e: It occurs only in plants and cyanobacteria. Some cyanobacteria can photosynthesize and also fix nitrogen.

q: It occurs in all living ____.
e: It occurs in all living organisms. Organisms is the biological term this statement needs.

q: It takes place in the presence of ____.
e: It takes place in the presence of light. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis.

q: It takes place throughout the ____.
e: It takes place throughout the day. Day is the biological term this statement needs.

q: It occurs in chloroplast and is dependent on ____.
e: It occurs in chloroplast and is dependent on light. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. Chloroplasts are the green organelles where photosynthesis happens.

q: Aerobic respiration occurs in cytoplasm and mitochondria and is independent on ____.
e: Aerobic respiration occurs in cytoplasm and mitochondria and is independent on light. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. Mitochondria are the organelles of aerobic respiration and ATP production.

q: It uses water and carbon ____.
e: It uses water and carbon dioxide. Dioxide is the biological term this statement needs.

q: It uses carbohydrates or organic substances and ____.
e: It uses carbohydrates or organic substances and oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: In this process, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in ____.
e: In this process, light energy is fixed in the form of chemical energy and stored in carbohydrates. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: In this process, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release ____.
e: In this process, chemical energy stored in carbohydrates burns to release energy. Living systems need a continual energy input to keep organised. Carbohydrates are sugars and polymers of sugars used for energy and structure.

q: Oxygen is liberated in this process and carbon dioxide is ____.
e: Oxygen is liberated in this process and carbon dioxide is utilized. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.

q: Oxygen is utilized and carbon dioxide is ____.
e: Oxygen is utilized and carbon dioxide is released. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.
